description: Four polyphonic low frequency oscillators, each with sine, triangle, sawtooth and square outputs, its own pulse width and its own clock input

params.text: Sets that oscillator's rate: unclocked it runs from 0.0039062Hz fully counter-clockwise to 1024Hz fully clockwise; with a clock patched it divides and multiplies that clock instead
Sets the width of that oscillator's square output, from 1% fully counter-clockwise to 99% fully clockwise; it comes up at 50%
Inverts that oscillator's output; in unipolar mode the inverted signal spans 0V to 10V as the uninverted one does
Switches that oscillator between 0V to 10V, which it comes up in, and -5V to +5V
Attenuverts the voltage at that oscillator's F.M. input before it is added to the FREQ knob; fully clockwise the input tracks one volt per octave
Attenuverts the voltage at that oscillator's P.W.M. input before it is added to the P.W. knob

inputs.text: A clock for that oscillator, read high above 2V and low below 0.1V; the oscillator locks its rate to the clock, though not its phase, and the FREQ knob becomes a divider and multiplier
A trigger above 2V returns that oscillator's phase to the start of its cycle
Shifts that oscillator's rate, scaled by the attenuverter beside it; this jack alone sets the section's polyphony, and its voltages are read one per channel
Shifts that oscillator's pulse width; the voltage is divided by 10, scaled by the attenuverter beside it and added to the P.W. knob, with the total held between 1% and 99%

outputs.text: A sine wave from that oscillator
A triangle wave from that oscillator
A sawtooth wave from that oscillator
A square wave from that oscillator, its width set by the P.W. knob

notes: A section is monophonic until a cable reaches its F.M. input: that jack alone sets how many channels the section runs, and every output follows it.
The four oscillators start a quarter of a cycle apart from one another.
A clock input is monophonic, so every channel of a section locks to the one clock.
